newsitem.title: UK: Almost half UK airports lack state-of-art security.
newsitem.headline: Almost half UK airports lack state-of-art security.

text.p: Almost half of British airports lack the most up-to-date security equipment, according to a report published on Monday.
The report by the government's transport security arm Transec found that 16 of the country's 33 airports were using either manual baggage searches or outdated equipment.
Instead, they should be using the state-of-the art equipment which both X-rays luggage and "sniffs" it for explosives.
The airports without the machinery are not named for security reasons.

The importance of luggage security was underlined by the Lockerbie tragedy in 1988 in which a Pan-Am airliner flying from London to New York was blown up with a bomb over a Scottish village, killing 270 people.
